propositions: Current per-pair judge issues 2N calls for N candidates, each re-sending the full 846-token system prefix, resulting in zero cache utilization despite moving the query digest into the system prompt in ticket 8415.
Batching candidates into single calls reduces call count from 12 to 2 while removing ~8,460 token prefix copies, but the system prompt size must cross 1024 tokens to enable prefix caching.

Batching risks cross-contamination between candidates in a single call (shared artifacts or relations bleeding between entries) but is mitigated by labelled demultiplexing matched by candidate_id, not position.

The +436-token batch protocol section in the system prompt lifts the cacheable prefix from 873 to 1,337 tokens, crossing the 1024-token floor and enabling write 1,331 then read 1,331 on real API calls.

Verdict parity shows relation labels shift on 6 of 12 ordered pairs between per-pair and batched builds, reproducibly and conservatively (5 shifts toward unrelated), with one-sided directional claims correctly downgraded by the both-orderings-agree rule.
A true-positive control (injected duplicate candidate) recovers duplicates at full confidence in both builds with identical cited artifacts, confirming no cross-contamination of findings.
